pageCache.text:
British Values and SMSC
At Oakdale Junior School spiritual, moral, social and cultural development (SMSC) underpins everything we do and this includes actively promoting British Values. We want our children to develop the wisdom to make social, moral and ethical decisions with reflection, empathy and intelligence. We believe all children can develop responsibility with respect for themselves and others; values and attitudes that will stand them in good stead as they become global citizens.
We want our children to aspire to be the best they can be. We develop a sense of social and moral responsibility fitting for the global society in which we live, through being a Rights Respecting School; a school where everyone is aware of their rights and responsibilities towards others. Our school community strives for a greater understanding of the contribution we can all make regardless of age, gender, race or religion by providing equal opportunities for all.
BRITISH VALUES AT OAKDALE JUNIOR SCHOOL
What are British values?
The document “Promoting fundamental British values as part of SMSC in schools” says “Schools should promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs”. It is this list of values that are used below as a basis for this statement.
Promoting British Values Oakdale Junior School
At Oakdale Junior School, the importance of SMSC education in developing well-rounded global citizens who contribute to society and improve their communities has always been recognised and promoted as integral to membership of the school. British fundamental values have always been at the heart of what we do. When the term ‘British’ values is used it is important to underline that this embraces the fact that we are a nation with a proud history of people of many different ethnic backgrounds, religious beliefs and secular values all living together in a plural society. Our school models this wider picture of inclusivity, freedom and equality, so our underpinning values are British to the core.
British Values and SMSC
How do we promote British Values at Oakdale?
SMSC stands for Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural education. It is not taught as a lesson, it is embedded across our curriculum; For example it could be part of Religious Education, Physical Education, English, History, Geography or Art. It is central to the ethos of the school which children experience on a daily basis. SMSC is now highlighted by government as a key means of promoting basic British Values and counteracting the development of religious extremism in some school settings.

Welcome
Welcome to Oakdale Junior School.
On behalf of the children, staff and Governors, it is with great pleasure that I welcome you to Oakdale Junior School which is part of The Oakdale Federation. We are a happy, vibrant and a successful community where every child is recognised as an individual.
Our aim is to provide an inspiring curriculum that helps prepare children to lead full and active lives in a rapidly changing world. We want our children to be prepared for each phase of their schooling (infants to junior or junior to secondary), as confident, resilient, curious and respectful young people, with high aspirations for themselves. We also want them to be prepared for a world that has yet to be invented or created so that they will be confident to take their part in society.
We see education as a partnership between school and home. In our experience, children are most likely to achieve their potential when parents/carers and teachers work together. We provide regular opportunities for parents to come into school, not only to discuss their child/ren’s academic progress or personal development, but also to share in other aspects of their wider education.
I hope that our website captures the essence of our school, however we encourage families and professionals to visit. We look forward to welcoming you to meet some of our children and staff and to experience, for yourself, the quality of education given to all our children. If you require further information, please do not hesitate to contact us.
EXECUTIVE HEADTEACHER
Oakdale Juniors is special - we are a happy, inclusive and successful school where staff care endlessly for pupils both academically and emotionally. We are proud to be a Gold Rights Respecting School and a Nurturing School as we know that by putting well-being and happiness first, children will achieve their very best in all areas of school life. Children have the right to an education that develops their personality, talents and abilities to their fullest potential and at Oakdale, we are committed to providing this opportunity. (Article 29 of the United Nation’s Convention on the Rights of the Child)
Our curriculum is exciting and prepares children for the part they will play in our rapidly changing world. They will learn inside and outside the classroom from dedicated teachers, support staff and visitors, ensuring that they know more, do more and remember more as they move through each year. We want children to be resilient, confident and curious about the world so that they have amazing aspirations for the future.
This prospectus and our website will give you a taster of our school, but please arrange a time to visit us and see our school at work and the extensive grounds we have to offer. Education is at it’s best when school and home work together, so we look forward to welcoming you to Oakdale.

Reading and Phonics
Reading and Phonics
Reading and Phonics at Oakdale
The reading curriculum at Oakdale, steeped in the arts and rooted in equity, allows our children to develop a rich vocabulary, so that they can delve deeply into more challenging and inspiring texts. With their skills in oracy, which are embedded our class texts, and their growing understanding of the world around them, our children feel empowered to take risks with their opinions and ideas, opening pathways for them to succeed in life. Our aim is to provide a nurturing and extensive platform, from which children can strive to remove barriers to success, and develop and acquire reading skills in a progressive, but holistic way. We are determined that every child will learn to read.
Reading is an interactive process that involves drawing upon knowledge and experience of the world, and being able to extract information, challenging views and opinions. The developing reader needs to acquire specific skills in order to make sense of the written word. These skills are inherent within our reading lessons, with the main emphasis on the child being able to develop their skills when reading challenging texts (for example summarising, clarifying, making predictions, skimming and scanning, visualising, describing and questioning).
Children have numerous opportunities to read independently, with partners, in groups and with the whole class. Leaders and teachers have high expectations of children’s reading and believe that children’s engagement of our inspiring texts has a direct impact on progress in oracy and writing.
We use Read Write Inc. to support the development of early reading skills for children who have not passed their phonics test in Key Stage 1 and for any children throughout the school that need support. This intervention provides a systematic and methodical approach to the teaching of phonics and an effective assessment to support progress. This scheme has been recommended as a validated systemic synthetic phonic programme by the DfE. This consistent and progressive programme takes place on a daily basis and is delivered by trained LSAs. It is monitored by our Assistant Head for Inclusion and our English Lead but all teaching staff have been trained in it's approach.

Year 4 Science Book Club
We once again have the opportunity to take part in judging the shortlist of books for the Royal Institution Young People's Book Prize. For more information about this, please click here: https://royalsociety.org/grants-schemes-awards/book-prizes/young-peoples-book-prize/
Here are some photos of some of the club enjoying science activities inspired by the books we've been reading and judging.
Year 4 Science Book Club
What the children think about science
A pupil voice survey taken of pupils across the school this week showed that children enjoy learning science at Oakdale and get to work practically most weeks.
Most children took part in some scientific activity during lockdown- whether this was making slime, watching videos on youtube, or testing out what floated and sank. In addition, they understand how the science we study in school is relevant to their lives. Children need more support to understand and practise scientific vocabulary, and more agency to plan and carry out investigations to answer their own questions, and this is what we will be working on next, as a school.

Extra-Curricular Visits and Visitors
The visits and visitors that we organise across the year are an incredibly important part of our curriculum. Educational visits and visitors have a positive impact on our pupils; stimulating interest, curiosity and a passion for learning. These experiences expose children to new cultures, provide opportunities to develop new skills and build new relationships, which ultimately prepare them for life beyond Oakdale. These special days are most importantly a fun way to learn and have such an impact, that they are likely to be the memories our pupils cherish as they move through both schools.
Extra-Curricular Visits and Visitors
Visits
These are the places we have visited this year in London and beyond! They may change from year to year as our curriculum evolves. We also try to visit a place of worship every year linked to the religion we are focusing on.
Visitors
Every term we also organise a visitor to come into school to speak to the children about a topic they are learning about. Again, these will vary but it is always a good opportunity to listen to an expert and make memories on these special days at school. Quite often these days will link to History, Geography or Science.
